title: THP-1 Differentiation & Polarization Protocol
text:
Configure experiment


Code
viewof vessel          = Inputs.select(["24-well", "6-well", "T-25", "T-175", "T-525"], {label: "Culture vessel", value: "6-well"})
viewof pma_final_nM    = Inputs.number({label: "PMA final concentration (nM)", value: 25, min: 1, step: 1})
viewof lps_final_ngmL  = Inputs.number({label: "LPS final concentration (ng/mL)", value: 10, min: 0.1, step: 0.5})
viewof ifng_final_ngmL = Inputs.number({label: "IFNγ final concentration (ng/mL)", value: 20, min: 0.1, step: 1})
viewof il4_final_ngmL  = Inputs.number({label: "IL-4 final concentration (ng/mL)", value: 25, min: 0.1, step: 1})
viewof il13_final_ngmL = Inputs.number({label: "IL-13 final concentration (ng/mL)", value: 25, min: 0.1, step: 1})
viewof stock_mult      = Inputs.number({label: "Stock-prep batch multiplier (× the standard recipe below)", value: 1, min: 0.1, step: 0.1})





















































Code
fmt = (x, d = 2) => x.toFixed(d)

vessel_table = ({
  "24-well": {mL: 1.0,   cells: 200000,    wells: 24, lps_dilution: "2x"},
  "6-well":  {mL: 5.0,   cells: 1000000,   wells: 6,  lps_dilution: "2x"},
  "T-25":    {mL: 12.5,  cells: 2500000,   wells: 1,  lps_dilution: "1x"},
  "T-175":   {mL: 92.0,  cells: 18400000,  wells: 1,  lps_dilution: "1x"},
  "T-525":   {mL: 276.0, cells: 55200000,  wells: 1,  lps_dilution: "1x"}
})

v = vessel_table[vessel]

md`**Vessel: ${vessel} (${fmt(v.mL,1)} mL, ~${v.cells.toLocaleString()} cells) · PMA ${pma_final_nM} nM · LPS ${lps_final_ngmL} ng/mL · IFNγ ${ifng_final_ngmL} ng/mL · IL-4 ${il4_final_ngmL} ng/mL · IL-13 ${il13_final_ngmL} ng/mL · stock batch ×${fmt(stock_mult,1)}**`




































TipReproducing the source calculator (math audit)





All volumes below are derived, never hardcoded, from the same relationship used in THP1_Polarization_Volumes.xlsx:
\[V_{stock\ to\ add\ (\mu L)} = \frac{C_{final} \times (V_{vessel,\ mL} \times 1000)}{C_{stock\ used}}\]
PMA’s stock concentration is back-calculated from mass and molarity:
\[C_{PMA\ stock} = \frac{mass\ (g)/volume\ (L)}{MW_{PMA}\ (616.83\ g/mol)}, \qquad C_{working} = \frac{C_{stock}}{10}\ \text{(1:10 dilution)}\]
LPS uses one of two serial 1:100 dilutions of its 1 mg/mL stock depending on vessel size — smaller vessels (24-well, 6-well) draw from the more dilute “2x dil” stock (100 ng/mL) so pipetting volumes stay reasonable; larger vessels (T-25/T-175/T-525) draw from the “1x dil” stock (10 µg/mL). This matches vessel_table.lps_dilution above.
Plugging in the defaults (6-well, PMA 25 nM, LPS 10 ng/mL, IFNγ 20 ng/mL) reproduces the source spreadsheet and THP1_Polarization_Protocol.docx’s printed table (7.72 µL PMA, 500 µL LPS, 10 µL IFNγ) exactly.

title: THP-1 Differentiation & Polarization Protocol
text:
Stock solution prep
Make once; store single-use aliquots at −20°C. Scale the whole batch with the multiplier above if you need more aliquots than the standard recipe yields.

PMA stock — 100 µg/mL (162 µM) in DMSO


Code
pma_MW              = 616.83
pma_mass_mg         = 1.0 * stock_mult
pma_dmso_mL         = 10.0 * stock_mult
pma_conc_gL         = pma_mass_mg / pma_dmso_mL           // mg/mL == g/L
pma_molarity_uM     = (pma_conc_gL / pma_MW) * 1000
pma_stock_aliquot_uL = 50
pma_stock_aliquots  = (pma_dmso_mL * 1000) / pma_stock_aliquot_uL

Inputs.table([
  {Component: "12-O-tetradecanoylphorbol-13-acetate (PMA), lyophilized", Amount: `${fmt(pma_mass_mg,1)} mg` },
  {Component: "Dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO)", Amount: `${fmt(pma_dmso_mL,1)} mL` },
  {Component: "Resulting stock concentration", Amount: `100 µg/mL (${fmt(pma_molarity_uM,1)} µM)` },
  {Component: "Single-use aliquots", Amount: `${fmt(pma_stock_aliquots,0)} aliquots of ${pma_stock_aliquot_uL} µL, −20°C` }
], {layout: "auto"})
































































TipWorking (1:10) PMA dilution





Per THP1_Polarization_Protocol.docx, the working dilution is made fresh in RPMI/FCS media (not DMSO) immediately before treating cells: 1:10 dilution of the 100 µg/mL stock in RPMI/FCS → 10 µg/mL working stock.





Code
pma_working_stock_nM = pma_molarity_uM * 1000 / 10   // 1:10 dilution, µM → nM

md`**Working PMA stock (1:10 in RPMI/FCS): ≈${fmt(pma_working_stock_nM,0)} nM** — this is the value used as $C_{stock}$ for the vessel calculator below.`


















LPS stock — 1 mg/mL in RPMI/FCS


Code
lps_mass_mg          = 10.0 * stock_mult
lps_rpmi_mL          = 10.0 * stock_mult
lps_conc_mgmL        = lps_mass_mg / lps_rpmi_mL
lps_stock_aliquot_uL = 500
lps_stock_aliquots   = (lps_rpmi_mL * 1000) / lps_stock_aliquot_uL

Inputs.table([
  {Component: "Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) from *Escherichia coli*, lyophilized", Amount: `${fmt(lps_mass_mg,1)} mg` },
  {Component: "RPMI/FCS media", Amount: `${fmt(lps_rpmi_mL,1)} mL` },
  {Component: "Resulting stock concentration", Amount: `${fmt(lps_conc_mgmL,2)} mg/mL` },
  {Component: "Single-use aliquots", Amount: `${fmt(lps_stock_aliquots,0)} aliquots of ${lps_stock_aliquot_uL} µL, −20°C` }
], {layout: "auto"})


















































TipWorking LPS dilutions (both made fresh in RPMI/FCS)





Two serial 1:100 dilutions from the 1 mg/mL stock, both in RPMI/FCS:





Code
lps_1x_ngmL = (lps_conc_mgmL / 100) * 1e6   // "1x dil" — mg/mL → ng/mL
lps_2x_ngmL = (lps_1x_ngmL / 100)            // "2x dil" — further 1:100 of the 1x dilution

Inputs.table([
  {Dilution: "Stock (1x 1:100 dilution)", "Concentration": `${fmt(lps_1x_ngmL/1000,1)} µg/mL (${fmt(lps_1x_ngmL,0)} ng/mL)`, "Used for": "T-25, T-175, T-525"},
  {Dilution: "Stock (2x 1:100 dilution)", "Concentration": `${fmt(lps_2x_ngmL,1)} ng/mL`,                                    "Used for": "24-well, 6-well"}
], {layout: "auto"})

























IFNγ (interferon gamma) stock — 10 µg/mL in PBS + BSA carrier






NoteBSA carrier concentration — flagged discrepancy





The source spreadsheet labels this carrier “PBS + 1% BSA,” but back-calculating from the docx recipe (100 µL of 20 mg/mL BSA into a 2.0 mL final volume) gives 2 mg BSA / 2.0 mL = 0.1% w/v, not 1%. The same 20 mg/mL BSA stock and dilution ratio is used for the IL-4 and IL-13 carriers below, which also work out to 0.1% w/v.






Code
ifng_mass_ug          = 20.0 * stock_mult
ifng_carrier_mL        = 2.0 * stock_mult
ifng_conc_ugmL         = ifng_mass_ug / ifng_carrier_mL
ifng_conc_ngmL         = ifng_conc_ugmL * 1000
ifng_small_aliquot_uL  = 20
ifng_large_aliquot_uL  = 200
ifng_small_aliquots    = (ifng_carrier_mL * 1000) / ifng_small_aliquot_uL

Inputs.table([
  {Component: "Recombinant human interferon gamma (IFNγ), lyophilized", Amount: `${fmt(ifng_mass_ug,1)} µg` },
  {Component: "PBS + BSA carrier (see note above)", Amount: `${fmt(ifng_carrier_mL,2)} mL` },
  {Component: "Resulting stock concentration", Amount: `${fmt(ifng_conc_ugmL,1)} µg/mL (${fmt(ifng_conc_ngmL,0)} ng/mL)` },
  {Component: "Single-use aliquots", Amount: `${fmt(ifng_small_aliquots,0)} aliquots of ${ifng_small_aliquot_uL} µL (or ${ifng_large_aliquot_uL} µL large aliquots), −20°C` }
], {layout: "auto"})


























































No further dilution is made — IFNγ is added to media directly from this stock.


IL-4 and IL-13 stocks — 10 µg/mL in PBS + BSA carrier (for M2 polarization)


Code
il4_mass_ug          = 5.0 * stock_mult
il4_carrier_mL       = 0.5 * stock_mult
il4_conc_ugmL        = il4_mass_ug / il4_carrier_mL
il4_conc_ngmL        = il4_conc_ugmL * 1000
il4_aliquot_uL       = 25
il4_aliquots         = (il4_carrier_mL * 1000) / il4_aliquot_uL

il13_mass_ug         = 2.0 * stock_mult
il13_carrier_mL      = 0.2 * stock_mult
il13_conc_ugmL       = il13_mass_ug / il13_carrier_mL
il13_conc_ngmL       = il13_conc_ugmL * 1000
il13_aliquot_uL      = 10
il13_aliquots        = (il13_carrier_mL * 1000) / il13_aliquot_uL

Inputs.table([
  {Component: "Recombinant human interleukin-4 (IL-4), lyophilized",  Amount: `${fmt(il4_mass_ug,1)} µg`,  "PBS + BSA carrier": `${fmt(il4_carrier_mL,2)} mL`,  "Stock conc.": `${fmt(il4_conc_ugmL,1)} µg/mL`,  Aliquots: `${fmt(il4_aliquots,0)} × ${il4_aliquot_uL} µL` },
  {Component: "Recombinant human interleukin-13 (IL-13), lyophilized", Amount: `${fmt(il13_mass_ug,1)} µg`, "PBS + BSA carrier": `${fmt(il13_carrier_mL,2)} mL`, "Stock conc.": `${fmt(il13_conc_ugmL,1)} µg/mL`, Aliquots: `${fmt(il13_aliquots,0)} × ${il13_aliquot_uL} µL` }
], {layout: "auto"})

text:
M0 differentiation (PMA)

Standard workflow — 6-well plate, 25 nM PMA (from THP1_Polarization_Protocol.docx)






ImportantBefore the experiment



Grow THP-1 cells to a density of 1×10⁶ cells/mL in RPMI/FCS media.




Code
Inputs.table([
  {Day: "Day 1", Step: "1", Action: `Add ${fmt(v.mL - (v.mL/5),1)} mL RPMI/FCS to each well` , Detail: `(4 mL/well at 6-well scale; scale by vessel)` },
  {Day: "Day 1", Step: "2", Action: "Dilute PMA 1:10 in RPMI/FCS (100 µg/mL stock → 10 µg/mL working)", Detail: "Fresh" },
  {Day: "Day 1", Step: "3", Action: `Add cell suspension to a final density of ~${v.cells.toLocaleString()} cells (${fmt(v.mL/5,2)} mL of 1×10⁶ cells/mL stock at 6-well scale)`, Detail: "Scale by vessel" },
  {Day: "Day 1", Step: "4", Action: `Once settled, treat immediately with ${fmt(pma_add_uL,2)} µL of 10 µg/mL PMA working stock (final ${pma_final_nM} nM); incubate 24 h`, Detail: "37°C, 5% CO₂" },
  {Day: "Day 2", Step: "5", Action: "Aspirate PMA-containing media; wash once with fresh RPMI/FCS (or PBS)", Detail: "—" },
  {Day: "Day 2", Step: "6", Action: `Add ${fmt(v.mL,1)} mL fresh RPMI/FCS`, Detail: "Rest period begins" },
  {Day: "Day 2", Step: "7", Action: "Let cells rest for 3 days before polarization", Detail: "Undisturbed, 37°C" }
], {layout: "auto"})













NoteAlternative final concentration noted in the source





THP1_Polarization_Protocol.docx also notes that for a 100 nM final PMA concentration (instead of the 25 nM default above), use 30.8 µL of the 10 µg/mL working stock at 6-well scale — consistent with the calculator above if you raise pma_final_nM to 100.





Legacy/flask-scale workflow (from Differentiation_THP1s.docx)






Note



This is an older, vessel-agnostic write-up (originally a fill-in-the-blank bench worksheet targeting T-175 flasks) that predates the 6-well/day-by-day standard above. The blanks in the original are answered here by the reactive calculator — select “T-175” in Configure experiment to match its materials list.

title: Thawing Protocol — Adherent Cells
text:
Complete media (10% FBS, 1% Penicillin/Streptomycin)






NoteMath audit





Base recipe: 500 mL base media + 50 mL FBS (10%) + 5 mL Penicillin/Streptomycin (0.9%), 555 mL total — scales linearly:
\[V_{base} = V_{batch} \times \frac{500}{555} \qquad V_{FBS} = V_{batch} \times \frac{50}{555} \qquad V_{P/S} = V_{batch} \times \frac{5}{555}\]





Code
media_base_mL = media_batch_mL * (500 / 555)
media_fbs_mL  = media_batch_mL * (50 / 555)
media_ps_mL   = media_batch_mL * (5 / 555)

Inputs.table([

], {layout: "auto"})

Configure swap record

TipReverse direction (96 → 384)





The source protocol documents the 384→96 direction only. The same physical steps apply in reverse (swap sample block, heated cover, and plate adapter back to the 384-well hardware) — substitute “384-well” for “96-well” throughout the steps below when reversing.

Configure qPCR run


Code
viewof n_samples        = Inputs.number({label: "Number of biological samples (excluding water controls)", value: 24, min: 1, step: 1})
viewof n_replicates      = Inputs.number({label: "Replicates per sample × gene (wells)", value: 2, min: 1, step: 1})

viewof n_genes           = Inputs.number({label: "Number of target genes (used only if names above are blank)", value: 3, min: 1, step: 1})
viewof n_water_controls  = Inputs.number({label: "No-template (water) control wells per gene", value: 2, min: 0, step: 1})
viewof excess            = Inputs.number({label: "Master mix excess multiplier", value: 1.25, min: 1, max: 2, step: 0.05})














































Code
fmt = (x, d = 2) => x.toFixed(d)

genes = gene_names_text.trim()
  ? gene_names_text.split(",").map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean)
  : Array.from({length: n_genes}, (_, i) => `Gene ${i + 1}`)

wells_per_gene = n_samples * n_replicates + n_water_controls
total_wells    = wells_per_gene * genes.length

md`**${n_samples} sample(s) × ${n_replicates} replicate(s) + ${n_water_controls} water control(s) = ${wells_per_gene} well(s)/gene × ${genes.length} gene(s) = ${total_wells} total well(s)** · excess ×${excess}`







































Code
total_wells > 96
  ? md`::: {.callout-warning}
**Exceeds one 96-well plate.** ${total_wells} total wells requested — split across multiple 96-well plates, or use a 384-well plate/block if your instrument supports it.
:::`
  : md``













TipExample use case from the source spreadsheet





The original qPCR_Sample_Sheet.xlsx worked example ran a 6-timepoint series (0h, 0.5h, 1h, 4h, 6h, 24h) across 3 CRISPR’d clones + 1 WT control, each in duplicate, against 3 genes (IL1B, β-Actin, AP-1/FOS) — i.e. 4 conditions × 6 timepoints = 24 samples, 2 replicates, 3 genes, plus water and extra controls. Reproduce that specific layout by setting samples = 24, replicates = 2, genes = “IL1B, B-Actin, AP-1”. This is mentioned as an example only — nothing about gene identity or timepoints is hardcoded into the calculator itself.









NoteMath audit — how every volume is calculated





Per-well TaqMan reaction (20 µL total, fixed ratio — single source of truth below):
\[V_{well} = V_{cDNA} + V_{probe} + V_{TaqMan\;MM} + V_{water} = 2 + 1 + 10 + 7 = 20\;\mu L\]
Wells needed per gene (includes water controls, which use the same master mix but 2 µL water instead of cDNA):
\[W_{gene} = N_{samples} \times N_{replicates} + N_{water\;controls}\]
Master mix per gene (primer/probe + TaqMan MM + water only — cDNA/water is pipetted directly into the well, not part of the master mix):
\[V_{component,\;total} = V_{component,\;well} \times W_{gene} \times excess\]
This reproduces the source spreadsheet’s EXCESS × replicates × SUM(per-well column) formula, generalized so replicates is a single user-supplied parameter (technical + biological wells per sample) rather than a second hardcoded multiplier layered on top of the per-well list.

Code
fmt = (x, d = 2) => x.toFixed(d)

n_reactions = n_samples * n_primer_sets + (include_neg_ctrl ? n_primer_sets : 0)
mm_scale    = n_reactions * (1 + excess_pct / 100)

TipSource example, generalized





The source document’s worked example was 5 CRISPR’d cell lines × 2 primer sets + 1 negative control per primer set = 10 reactions across 2 master mixes, scaled exactly ×6 with no additional overage. That specific layout is reproduced here as the calculator’s defaults (5 samples, 2 primer sets, negative control on, 0% overage) — everything scales from n_samples, n_primer_sets, and excess_pct above rather than being hardcoded, so this works for any sample/primer-set count.

Primer prep






NoteMath audit — 100 µM resuspension volume





Lyophilized IDT primers are resuspended to 100 µM using the standard IDT relationship:
\[V_{IDTE\;(\mu L)} = nmol_{primer} \times 10\]






Code
viewof primer_nmol = Inputs.number({label: "Primer yield (nmol, from tube/Certificate of Analysis)", value: 30, min: 1, step: 0.1})









Code
idte_vol_100uM = primer_nmol * 10

md`**Add ${fmt(idte_vol_100uM)} µL IDTE** to reach a 100 µM stock for a ${primer_nmol} nmol primer tube.`

















Spin primer tubes down briefly in a mini centrifuge before opening.
Add the calculated IDTE volume; vortex briefly; let sit on the bench ~2–5 min.
Label with date and “100 µM.”
Make a 10 µM working stock: add 90 µL nuclease-free water + 10 µL of the 100 µM stock (10× dilution) to a labeled 1.5 mL DNA LoBind tube.

Master mix






TipReagent order





Add master mix components to each tube on ice, in the order listed below.





Code
viewof rxn_vol_uL = Inputs.number({label: "Final reaction volume (µL)", value: 20, min: 10, max: 50, step: 1})








```{ojs}

  {Component: "5X Phire Reaction Buffer", "Per reaction (µL)": 4},
  {Component: "10 mM dNTPs (deoxynucleotide triphosphates)", "Per reaction (µL)": 0.4},
  {Component: "Forward Primer (10 µM)",   "Per reaction (µL)": 1},

mm_rows   = [...base_components, ...(use_dmso ? [dmso_component] : []), pol_component]
mm_per_rxn = mm_rows.reduce((s, r) => s + r["Per reaction (µL)"], 0)

Inputs.table(
  mm_rows
    .map(r => ({ ...r, [`${fmt(mm_scale, 2)}× + overage (µL)`]: fmt(r["Per reaction (µL)"] * mm_scale) }))
    .concat([{ Component: "Total master mix (per reaction)", "Per reaction (µL)": fmt(mm_per_rxn), [`${fmt(mm_scale, 2)}× + overage (µL)`]: fmt(mm_per_rxn * mm_scale) }]),
  { layout: "auto" }
)
```

NoteMath audit — template DNA and water-to-volume





The source document leaves template volume as “Xul,” to be filled in after measuring each sample’s DNA concentration. This calculator derives it directly instead of leaving it blank:
\[V_{template} = \frac{mass_{target}\;(ng)}{C_{DNA}\;(ng/\mu L)} \qquad V_{water} = V_{rxn} - V_{MM} - V_{template}\]

viewof dna_conc_ngul   = Inputs.number({label: "Your DNA stock concentration (ng/µL)", value: 50, min: 0.1, step: 0.1})

title: iPSC Culture Protocol
text:
Matrigel coating






TipWhy the aliquot volume isn’t a fixed number





Matrigel’s protein concentration varies lot to lot, so the volume of a thawed aliquot needed to reach a given final concentration is lot-dependent. Enter your current lot’s stock concentration below (from its Certificate of Analysis) and the calculator derives the correct aliquot volume — never assume a previous lot’s number still applies.





Code
viewof matrigel_target_mgmL = Inputs.number({label: "Target final Matrigel concentration (mg/mL) — 0.35 for iPSC, 1.0 for microglia differentiation", value: 0.35, min: 0.05, step: 0.05})
viewof matrigel_lot_mgmL    = Inputs.number({label: "Matrigel lot stock concentration (mg/mL, from Certificate of Analysis)", value: 9.0, min: 1, step: 0.1})


















Code
matrigel_soln_mL_per_well = 1.5
matrigel_total_soln_mL    = matrigel_soln_mL_per_well * n_wells
matrigel_aliquot_mL       = matrigel_target_mgmL * matrigel_total_soln_mL / matrigel_lot_mgmL
matrigel_dmemf12_mL       = matrigel_total_soln_mL - matrigel_aliquot_mL

Inputs.table([
  {Component: "Total coating solution needed", Amount: `${fmt(matrigel_total_soln_mL,2)} mL (${matrigel_soln_mL_per_well} mL/well × ${n_wells} wells)`},
  {Component: "Matrigel aliquot to thaw",       Amount: `${fmt(matrigel_aliquot_mL,3)} mL`},
  {Component: "DMEM/F12 to dilute to volume",   Amount: `${fmt(matrigel_dmemf12_mL,2)} mL`}
], {layout: "auto"})











































NotemTeSR1 Certificate-of-Analysis shortcut





If using with mTeSR1 media, the manual’s own example aliquot size is typically 270–350 µL per 25 mL DMEM/F12 — follow the dilution factor printed on that lot’s Certificate of Analysis rather than the calculator above if the two disagree.




Making single-use Matrigel aliquots







Day
Step




−1
Thaw Matrigel by submerging the vial in ice, in a 4°C fridge, overnight. Pre-cool tubes and pipette tips.


0
Swirl the thawed vial to disperse evenly; keep on ice. Spray the Matrigel container and ice bucket with 70% ethanol before placing in the hood. Switch tips/pipettes whenever Matrigel clogs. Refreeze aliquots immediately after making them.









TipSizing aliquots for different final concentrations





Per Justin Brumbaugh: for standard iPSC culture, freeze pure Matrigel aliquots sized to coat 2× 6-well plates at 1.5 mL/well, final 0.35 mg/mL. For microglia differentiation, the iPSC-to-Microglia 2.0 paper’s protocol uses 1 mg/mL final — size aliquots accordingly using the calculator above with matrigel_target_mgmL set to 1.0.





Using a Matrigel aliquot to coat plates







Day
Step




−1
Thaw one aliquot on ice in a 4°C fridge overnight. Pre-cool tips/pipettes.


0
Add the aliquot to the calculated volume of DMEM/F12 (table above) to reach the target concentration. Spread 1.5 mL Matrigel solution per well of a 6-well plate with a pre-cooled pipette (switch pipette if clogging). Incubate the coated plate at room temperature (15–25°C) for ≥1 hour before use.









WarningDo not scratch the coating



Aspirate the remaining liquid just before use, taking care that the pipette tip does not scratch the coated surface. Store coated plates with the liquid still on (not aspirated) in the incubator for up to 1 week, or until dry patches start to appear — do not store in the fridge, as its gas environment differs from the incubator.

text:
Thawing






Important1 hour before, or the day before



Coat 2 wells of a 6-well plate with Matrigel (see above) per cryovial being thawed.




Code
viewof dropwise_teSR_mL_per_vial = Inputs.number({label: "Warm TeSR-E8 added dropwise per vial (mL, source range 5–7)", value: 6, min: 5, max: 7, step: 0.5})









Code
thaw_dropwise_total_mL = dropwise_teSR_mL_per_vial * n_vials
thaw_resuspend_total_mL = 1 * n_vials
thaw_wells_needed = 2 * n_vials

Inputs.table([
  {Item: "Wells to pre-coat with Matrigel", Amount: `${thaw_wells_needed} wells (2/vial)`},
  {Item: "Warm TeSR-E8 for dropwise addition", Amount: `${fmt(thaw_dropwise_total_mL,1)} mL (${dropwise_teSR_mL_per_vial} mL/vial × ${n_vials} vial(s))`},
  {Item: "TeSR-E8 for pellet resuspension", Amount: `${fmt(thaw_resuspend_total_mL,1)} mL (1 mL/vial)`}
], {layout: "auto"})





































Step
Action




1
Have tubes, warmed TeSR-E8, and pre-coated plates ready before starting — work quickly.


2
Quickly thaw the cryovial in a 37°C water bath (actual water, not a bead bath) by continuously gently shaking until only a small frozen pellet remains.


3
Remove from bath; wipe with 70% ethanol.


4
Use a 2 mL serological pipette (not a 1 mL pipettor) to transfer cryovial contents to a 15 mL conical tube.


5
Add warm TeSR-E8 dropwise (volume above), gently mixing.


6
Centrifuge 300×g, 5 min, RT.


7
Aspirate medium, leaving the pellet intact; gently resuspend in 1 mL TeSR-E8 with a 2 mL serological pipette — maintain aggregates but break up big chunks (unbroken chunks promote differentiation). Don’t pipette the whole volume up/down; avoid bubbles.


8
Transfer 0.5 mL cell mixture per well of the pre-coated plate (2 wells/vial). More aggregates are needed post-thaw than during routine passaging.


9
Place the plate in the 37°C incubator; move in quick, short back-and-forth/side-to-side motions to distribute aggregates, then do not disturb for 24 hours.









TipDay 1 onward





Perform daily medium changes with TeSR-E8, visually assessing growth/differentiation until the next passage. Manual colony selection may be needed the next day or after 2 days to remove differentiated cells. Undifferentiated (dense-centered) colonies may be ready to passage ~1–2 days post-thaw.
If a lot of single-cell differentiation is seen, collect everything into a Falcon tube and spin 200×g for 30 sec — aggregates pellet while single differentiated cells stay in the supernatant; discard the supernatant and culture the pellet (per Justin Brumbaugh).
If only a few undifferentiated colonies are seen post-thaw, it may be necessary to select only those colonies and replate them (without splitting) into a same-size well on a newly coated plate (per the TeSR manual).
Once ready to split: Justin’s ratio is 1:4–1:8 every 2–3 days; Rose’s ratio is ~1:12 (1 well expanded into 12 wells of a 6-well plate). Cells are usable for experiments or freezing once healthy — normally after ≥2 splits.

title: iPSC Culture Protocol
text:
Passaging
Passage every time cells are ready (dense, undifferentiated colonies) — respect the 15/45 incubator rule above throughout.

Method A — EDTA
EDTA dissociation buffer (500 mL batch, store 4°C):



Component
Amount




0.5 M EDTA, pH ~7.4
500 µL


NaCl
0.9 g


Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺-free PBS (Invitrogen #14190)
to 500 mL



Sterilize by filtration.


Code
edta_rinse_mL_per_well = 1
edta_sit_mL_per_well   = 1.5
edta_neutralize_mL_per_well = 4

Inputs.table([
  {Step: "Rinse ×2 (wash out Mg²⁺/Ca²⁺)", "Per well": `${edta_rinse_mL_per_well} mL`, Total: `${fmt(edta_rinse_mL_per_well * n_wells,1)} mL per rinse (×2 rinses)`},
  {Step: "3rd EDTA addition — let sit 4–5 min", "Per well": `${edta_sit_mL_per_well} mL`, Total: `${fmt(edta_sit_mL_per_well * n_wells,1)} mL`},
  {Step: "Neutralize with fresh media (max pipetting speed)", "Per well": `${edta_neutralize_mL_per_well} mL`, Total: `${fmt(edta_neutralize_mL_per_well * n_wells,1)} mL`}
], {layout: "auto"})





































Step
Action




1
Have a Matrigel-coated plate ready; warm TeSR-E8 and EDTA dissociation media to RT (do not warm TeSR-E8 in a 37°C bath).


2
Optionally mark/remove differentiated colonies in the morning (respect the 15/45 incubator rule).


3
Rinse wells with room-temp EDTA medium (table above) to wash out Mg²⁺/Ca²⁺; discard.


4
Repeat the rinse once more.


5
Add EDTA medium a third time (table above); let sit 4–5 min (longer → tiny 3–5-cell colonies; a first split off feeders may need more time). During the wait, aspirate marked differentiated colonies by inclining the plate and vacuuming gently with a glass pipette — careful not to break the Matrigel coat; incline back between colonies to keep EDTA covering the plate and avoid drying. Endpoint cue: a hazy appearance by eye, or colony edges visibly peeling under the scope.


6
Aspirate the EDTA; add neutralizing media (table above) at max pipetting speed to gently disperse cells — Mg²⁺/Ca²⁺ in the media neutralizes the EDTA. Do not scrape cells off the bottom (causes differentiation/death).


7
Mix the suspension gently; plate at the desired split ratio (1:4 to 1:8); discard unused suspension.


8
Place in the incubator; rock back-and-forth/side-to-side to distribute; let sit undisturbed overnight for maximum attachment.









NoteCitation for this method





Chen G, Gulbranson DR, Hou Z, Bolin JM, Ruotti V, Probasco MD, Smuga-Otto K, Howden SE, Diol NR, Propson NE, Wagner R, Lee GO, Antosiewicz-Bourget J, Teng JMC, Thomson JA. “Chemically defined conditions for human iPS cell derivation and culture.” Nature Methods. 2011 Apr 10;8(4):424–429.





Method B — ReLeSR
ReLeSR is an enzyme-free reagent for aggregate dissociation without manual colony selection or scraping — recommended when first culturing a new line in TeSR-E8. Volumes below are per 1 well of a 6-well plate, scaled by n_wells.


Code
relesr_wash_mL_per_well = 1
relesr_reagent_mL_per_well = 1
relesr_teSR_mL_per_well = 1

Inputs.table([
  {Step: "D-PBS wash", "Per well": `${relesr_wash_mL_per_well} mL`, Total: `${fmt(relesr_wash_mL_per_well * n_wells,1)} mL`},
  {Step: "ReLeSR (aspirate within 1 min, leave thin film)", "Per well": `${relesr_reagent_mL_per_well} mL`, Total: `${fmt(relesr_reagent_mL_per_well * n_wells,1)} mL`},
  {Step: "TeSR-E8 to detach colonies", "Per well": `${relesr_teSR_mL_per_well} mL`, Total: `${fmt(relesr_teSR_mL_per_well * n_wells,1)} mL`}
], {layout: "auto"})





































Step
Action




1
Coat new plates with Matrigel ≥1 h before passaging; warm TeSR-E8 to RT (not a 37°C bath).


2
Wash cells with D-PBS (table above); aspirate. No need to remove differentiated regions first.


3
Add ReLeSR (table above); aspirate again within 1 minute, leaving colonies with just a thin film.


4
Incubate at RT for 7–9 min — optimal time is line-dependent; determine empirically the first time using a new line.


5
Add TeSR-E8 (table above). Detach colonies by holding the plate with one hand and firmly tapping the side with the other for ~30–60 sec.


6
Gently transfer to a 15 mL conical tube; centrifuge 300×g, 5 min, RT. Wipe the vial with 70% ethanol during the spin.


7
Aspirate supernatant without disturbing the pellet; resuspend in TeSR-E8 using a 2 mL serological pipette, gently, avoiding bubbles.


8
If colonies are too big, pipette up/down 2–3× (5 mL serological pipette in a conical, or once directly in the well) to break to ~50–200 µm aggregates.


9
Plate the aggregate mixture onto pre-coated wells containing TeSR-E8 at the desired density — cultures can typically be split every 4–7 days at 1:10 to 1:50 (Justin recommends 1:4–1:8, Rose recommends ~1:12); adjust ratio at the next passage if colonies were too dense or sparse.


10
Place in the 37°C incubator; quick short back-and-forth/side-to-side motions to distribute; do not disturb for 24 hours.


11
Perform daily medium changes with TeSR-E8; monitor growth/differentiation. If a colony shows any differentiated cells, remove the whole colony (as in the EDTA method’s colony-removal step).









WarningAmbiguity flagged in the source document



iPSC_Passaging.docx’s ReLeSR section describes, immediately after colony detachment and centrifugation, resuspending the pellet “in cold (2–8°C) CryoStor CS10… minimize aggregate breakup” — which is a freezing step, not a continued-culture passaging step. It is unclear whether this paragraph in the source was meant to describe (a) passaging cells forward into a new plate (in which case the pellet should be resuspended in TeSR-E8, not CryoStor, as presented in Steps 7–9 above), or (b) an abbreviated pointer to the freezing workflow that happens to follow the same detachment steps.

Freezing
Cryopreserve at the normal passaging timepoint. Each vial = aggregates from 1 well of a 6-well plate (CryoStor method) or half a well (EDTA method) — adjust for other cultureware. Use 2 mL pipettes, not tips, to avoid disrupting aggregates.

Method A — EDTA and DMSO


Code

freeze_edta_teSR_mL_per_well = 1     // TeSR-E8 added dropwise, per well
freeze_edta_vials_per_well   = 2     // final DMSO 10%

freeze_edta_teSR_total_mL = freeze_edta_teSR_mL_per_well * n_wells

], {layout: "auto"})


























































Step
Action




1
Aliquot TeSR-E8 and EDTA dissociation media; warm both to RT (do not warm TeSR-E8 in a 37°C bath).


2
Prep supplies: Mr. Frosty freezing container, labeled cryovials (table above), 20% DMSO-in-TeSR-E8, and normal TeSR-E8.


3
Optionally mark differentiated colonies in the morning (respect the 15/45 incubator rule).


4
Wash with EDTA dissociation media ×2 to fully remove Mg²⁺/Ca²⁺; discard.


5
Add EDTA media a third time; let sit 4–5 min (longer → tiny 3–5-cell colonies). During the wait, aspirate marked differentiated colonies as in the Passaging (EDTA) section above.


6
Aspirate EDTA; add TeSR-E8 at max speed to gently disperse cells; transfer gently to a 15 mL conical (careful not to over-break colonies — Mg²⁺/Ca²⁺ now neutralizes the EDTA). Do not scrape cells off the bottom.


7
Centrifuge 300×g, 5 min, RT. Wipe the vial with 70% ethanol before opening, during the spin.


8
Gently aspirate supernatant without disturbing the pellet; resuspend in 20% DMSO-in-TeSR-E8 (table above) using a 2 mL serological pipette, minimizing aggregate breakup, gentle, avoiding bubbles.


9
Add TeSR-E8 (table above) dropwise; mix once gently up/down; transfer 1 mL per cryovial (2 vials/well, final DMSO concentration 10%).


10
Freeze in a Mr. Frosty at −80°C overnight; transfer to liquid N₂ the next day.

], {layout: "auto"})



















































Step
Action

Aliquot and warm TeSR-E8 to RT (not a 37°C bath).


2
Wash with D-PBS (table above); aspirate — no need to remove differentiated regions.


3
Add ReLeSR (table above); aspirate within 1 min, leaving a thin film.


4

text:
Scaled master mixes






NoteMath audit — how every volume is calculated





Core formula (all standard mixes):
\[V_{total} = V_{per\_sample} \times N_{samples} \times 1.10\]
Formaldehyde crosslinking — working backwards from 1% final in ~10 mL/sample:
\[V_{16\%\;stock} = \frac{N_{cells} \times 1.1}{0.16} \; mL\]
Glycine quench — to reach 0.2M final from 2M stock:
\[V_{2M\;glycine} = \frac{N_{cells} \times 1.1}{10} \; mL\]
Biotin fill-in — ⚠️ 5% excess ONLY (not 10%):
\[V_{total} = V_{per\_sample} \times N_{samples} \times \mathbf{1.05}\]
Biotin-14-dATP costs ~$800/vial. The 5% exception is intentional and hardcoded.

Day 1 — Lysis & MboI restriction digest (~2 hr + O/N)






WarningMboI handling



Keep MboI in the glycerol block on ice at all times. Return to –20°C immediately after dispensing. Never let it sit at room temperature — glycerol-containing enzymes lose activity quickly when warmed.








NoteWhy 0.5% SDS + Triton X-100 quench?





SDS permeabilizes nuclei to allow MboI access to chromatin. However, SDS also inhibits MboI, so it must be quenched with Triton X-100 before adding enzyme. The 62°C step ensures denaturation of surface proteins without denaturing chromatin structure.

—

—

37°C 15 min; avoid foaming

text:
Day 2 — Biotin fill-in, ligation & crosslink reversal (~6.5 hr + O/N)






Warning5% excess only for biotin fill-in — not 10%



Biotin-14-dATP is extremely expensive. The biotin fill-in master mix uses 5% excess (not the standard 10%). This is the only step in the protocol with a different excess factor.








NoteWhy proximity ligation at RT with slow rotation?





Proximity ligation must occur while chromatin is still condensed inside intact nuclei — this ensures only DNA ends that are spatially close get ligated. Elevated temperature or vigorous mixing would release chromatin and allow random intermolecular ligation, destroying the contact information.

37°C 1.5h rotation

Slowest oven speed; door open

—

text:
Day 4 — Shearing & size selection (~6.5 hr)






WarningTarget size is 300–500 bp — verify with gel before proceeding



If shearing is outside this range, the size selection will be off and library complexity will suffer. Run a 1:5 dilution on a 2% agarose gel before proceeding to AMPure. Do not skip the gel check.








TipAMPure size selection logic

Stock solutions






NoteMath audit — how every volume is calculated





All four working buffers scale linearly off the source recipe’s own ratio, preserving each stated final concentration:
\[V_{component} = V_{batch} \times \frac{V_{component,\ source}}{V_{total,\ source}}\]

Blocking buffer (2% BSA in PBS): 1 g BSA / 50 mL → BSA (g) \(= 0.02 \times V_{batch}\)
Wash buffer (0.05% Tween-20 in PBS): 25 µL Tween-20 / 50 mL → Tween-20 (µL) \(= 0.5 \times V_{batch}\)
Permeabilization solution (0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS, from 10% stock): 2.5 mL 10% Triton stock / 50 mL → stock (mL) \(= 0.05 \times V_{batch}\)
4% formaldehyde fixative (from 16% stock): 10 mL 16% stock / 40 mL → stock (mL) \(= 0.25 \times V_{batch}\)
0.1% BSA in PBS (diluent): 0.5 g BSA / 500 mL → BSA (g) \(= 0.001 \times V_{diluent}\)




Blocking buffer (2% BSA in 1X PBS)


Code
block_bsa_g = 0.02 * batch_vol_mL
block_pbs_mL = batch_vol_mL * (49 / 50)   // preserves the source's 49 mL PBS : 1 g BSA : 50 mL total ratio

Antibody master mixes






NoteMath audit — antibody master mixes





Both dilutions scale directly with the number of wells, at the source’s stated per-well volumes (no additional pipetting excess is specified for either antibody step in the source):
\[V_{Ab} = V_{Ab,\ per\ well} \times N_{wells} \qquad V_{diluent} = V_{diluent,\ per\ well} \times N_{wells}\]
Primary: 1:100 dilution, 2 µL antibody + 198 µL 0.1% BSA/PBS per well (200 µL/well total) — matches the source’s 6-well worked example (12 µL Ab + 1188 µL diluent) exactly.
Secondary: 1:2000 dilution, stated as “0.1 µL antibody + 200 µL diluent, 200 µL per well” — but 0.1 + 200 = 200.1, not 200. The source’s own 25-well worked example (2.5 µL Ab + 4997 µL diluent) only reconciles if the per-well diluent is actually 199.9 µL (200 µL total − 0.1 µL antibody), which is what’s used below so that each well totals exactly 200 µL.

text:
Dilution calculators






NoteMath audit — both formulas are stated directly in the source protocol, not derived





To remove some media and replace with new media (you keep a portion of the current suspension and top it up to a target final volume at a target density):
\[C_1 V_1 = C_2 V_2\]

\(C_1\) = current cell density (from count)
\(C_2\) = desired cell density
\(V_2\) = desired final volume
Solve for \(V_1\) — the volume of current suspension to keep. Media to add = \(V_2 - V_1\).

\[V_1 = \frac{C_2 V_2}{C_1}\]
To add fresh media without removing any old media (top-up in place):
\[\frac{C_1}{V_1} = \frac{C_2}{V_2}\]

\(C_1\) = current cell density
\(V_1\) = volume of current cell media (your known, current volume — “leave this as V” per the source)
\(C_2\) = desired cell density
Solve for \(V_2\) — the volume of fresh media to add.

\[V_2 = \frac{C_2 V_1}{C_1}\]





Calculator 1 — remove & replace media (C₁V₁ = C₂V₂)


Code
viewof calcA_c1 = Inputs.number({label: "C1 — current density (×10⁵ cells/mL)", value: 8, min: 0.01, step: 0.1})
viewof calcA_c2 = Inputs.number({label: "C2 — desired density (×10⁵ cells/mL)", value: 4, min: 0.01, step: 0.1})
viewof calcA_v2 = Inputs.number({label: "V2 — desired final volume (mL)", value: 10, min: 0.1, step: 0.5})

























Code
calcA_v1 = (calcA_c2 * calcA_v2) / calcA_c1
calcA_media_to_add = calcA_v2 - calcA_v1

calcA_v1 > calcA_v2
  ? md`::: {.callout-warning}
**Not achievable.** Solving gives $V_1$ = ${fmt(calcA_v1)} mL, which exceeds the desired final volume ($V_2$ = ${fmt(calcA_v2)} mL) — your current density is already at or below the target. Lower $C_2$, raise $V_2$, or just add fresh media directly (Calculator 2) instead.
:::`
  : Inputs.table([
      {Quantity: "Keep this much of your current suspension (V1)", "Volume (mL)": fmt(calcA_v1)},
      {Quantity: "Top up with fresh media", "Volume (mL)": fmt(calcA_media_to_add)},
      {Quantity: "Final volume (V2)", "Volume (mL)": fmt(calcA_v2)}
    ], {layout: "auto"})

























Calculator 2 — top up without removing media (C₁/V₁ = C₂/V₂)


Code

RNA input calculator






NoteMath audit — how the RNA/water volumes are calculated





The source protocol reads: “Calculate the volume of RNA needed for 1g and add water to 15µl final volume” — “1g” is almost certainly a typo for 1 µg (a target RNA mass of 1 gram is not physically sensible for a bench RNA extraction; 1 µg is the standard iScript input and matches the embedded calculator spreadsheet found inside the source .docx, which computes =1000/[conc. ng/µL] — i.e. µL needed for 1000 ng = 1 µg). This is corrected below; flagging visibly per house convention rather than silently changing the source or preserving the apparent error.
\[V_{RNA} = \frac{Mass_{target}\;(ng)}{C_{RNA}\;(ng/\mu L)} \qquad V_{water} = V_{final} - V_{RNA}\]
If \(V_{RNA} > V_{final}\), the target mass is not reachable at that final volume and concentration — dilute less, use more RNA-concentrated input, or accept a lower input mass.

Working solutions — scaled to sample count






NoteMath audit — how every volume is calculated





CitraHB Complete (10 mL aliquot per sample — used in Steps 2, 3, and 6):
\[V_{aliquot} = 10\;mL \times N_{samples} \times (1 + overage)\]
Additives (SUPERase, RNAsin, spermidine, spermine, DTT) scale linearly with \(V_{aliquot}\); protease inhibitor tablets are whole units, so the tablet count rounds up.
Iodixanol step gradient — each of the three working solutions is made by diluting 50% iodixanol (itself made 5 parts OptiPrep : 1 part Diluent, since OptiPrep ships at 60% and \(5/6 \times 60\% = 50\%\)) down to the target percentage with CitraPrepHB, using \(C_1V_1 = C_2V_2\):
\[V_{50\%\ stock\ needed} = V_{total} \times \frac{\%_{target}}{50\%} \qquad V_{diluent} = V_{total} - V_{50\%\ stock\ needed}\]
Per-sample total volumes (from the source calculation): 15 mL of 50% (kept as-is), 4 mL of 40%, and 7.5 mL of 30%. All three scale with \(N_{samples} \times (1+overage)\).
Polyamine additives in each gradient solution scale as \(V_{total}/1000\) (spermidine, spermine, DTT — 1000X). SUPERase and RNAsin scale as:
\[V_{stock} = \frac{C_{final}}{C_{stock}} \times V_{total}\]
Each inhibitor’s \(C_{final}\) and the shared \(C_{stock}\) are set in Configure experiment (superase_final, rnasin_final, rnase_stock; defaults 0.5 / 0.5 / 40 U/µL). Change them there and every table below rescales.

Nuclei resuspension buffer (30 mL aliquot per sample):
\[V_{buffer} = 30\;mL \times N_{samples} \times (1+overage)\]
Bovine Serum Albumin (BSA) scales as 1% w/v of \(V_{buffer}\); SUPERase and RNAsin use the same \(C_{final}/C_{stock} \times V_{buffer}\) formula above. No spermine, spermidine, or Dithiothreitol (DTT) — these interfere with downstream cDNA synthesis.

title: CitraPrep Nuclei Isolation Protocol
text:
Protocol

Tissue homogenization (~30 min)






TipCheck nuclei before proceeding





Step 4 calls for pulling an aliquot to check nuclei release after homogenization — add more strokes with the tight pestle if intact cells are still visible before moving on.











Step
Action
Volume




1
Pre-chill 7 mL glass dounce homogenizer on ice
—


2
Cut snap-frozen tissue into small pieces (<0.5 cm) with clean scissors, in a petri dish on ice, in CitraHB complete
1 mL/sample


3
Transfer to dounce homogenizer on ice; add CitraHB complete; incubate 7 min on ice
4 mL/sample


4
Homogenize 20× with loose pestle; add Detergent; homogenize 20× with tight pestle. Pull an aliquot to check nuclei; homogenize further if needed
320 µL/sample Detergent


5
Filter through 40 µM strainer
—





Iodixanol gradient centrifugation (~1 hr + spin)

Mix the nuclei suspension with filtered trypan blue at a 1:1 ratio (e.g. 10 µL suspension + 10 µL trypan blue) — dilution factor = 2.
Load 10 µL of the mix onto the hemocytometer; let it wick in by capillary action, no bubbles.
Under the microscope, count nuclei in the 4 corner grid squares (16 small squares each). Use the standard hemocytometer counting rule: count nuclei touching the top and left borders of a square, but not the bottom or right, to avoid double-counting nuclei that sit on a line.

A Chromium Single Cell 3’ Gene Expression Dual Index library is a standard Illumina paired-end construct beginning and ending with P5 and P7. text:
iPSC maintenance phase (Day 0–11)






ImportantUses mTeSR1 + Thiazovivin — not plain TeSR-E8



The microglia-differentiation-track iPSCs in this protocol are maintained in mTeSR™1 (STEMCELL cat#: 5990/85857) with Thiazovivin (a ROCK inhibitor, 1000X aliquot, 1 µL/mL final) added to media used for thawing and splitting — not the plain TeSR™-E8 used in the base iPSC culture protocol. For Matrigel coating, thawing mechanics, and general passaging technique, see that page — it is not repeated here.



The 15/45-minute incubator rule from the base iPSC protocol applies here too.

Day 5 / Day 10 — “Splitting” step (distinct from full passaging)
This track’s outline calls for a lighter-weight splitting step at Day 5 and Day 10 (scan/scrape bad colonies, lift with mTeSR1 + Thiazovivin, replate at 1–2 new densities) rather than the full EDTA passage described in the base protocol:


Code
split_thiazovivin_uL_per_mL = 1   // 1000X, 1 µL/mL final
Inputs.table([

  {Step: "2", Action: "Vacuum DMEM/F12 from Matrigel-coated wells; add 1 mL/well mTeSR1 + 1x Thiazovivin so wells don't dry out", Detail: "—"},
  {Step: "3", Action: "Scan wells; mark and scrape bad colonies", Detail: "—"},
  {Step: "4", Action: "Vacuum media; rinse with 2 mL PBS/EDTA and aspirate", Detail: "—"},
  {Step: "5", Action: "Add 2 mL new PBS/EDTA; incubate 3–5 min", Detail: "Longer if plate is less crowded"},
  {Step: "6", Action: "Carefully vacuum PBS/EDTA without disturbing cells", Detail: "—"},
  {Step: "7", Action: "Add 1 mL mTeSR1 + 1x Thiazovivin (wide-tip 1000 µL tip); pipette up/down to lift cells into the 15 mL conical; repeat as needed", Detail: "A little roughness is OK if cells resist lifting, but not too much"},
  {Step: "8", Action: "Add 1 mL of cell mixture to each new well; move plate in a + shape (not circular) to mix", Detail: "—"},
  {Step: "9", Action: "Add 1 mL fresh mTeSR1 to the original well; return to incubator; do not open incubator for the rest of the day", Detail: "—"}
], {layout: "auto"})






















TipAttributed notes





Note from Isha: Day 1 after plating, the iPSCs are usually very stressed, so a media change will suffice. Scanning and scraping for bad colonies should start on Day 2. This note applies to the iPSC splits as well — the more crowded the plate, the easier it is to pick up the cells.
Note from Justin: If a lot of single-cell differentiation is seen, collect everything into a Falcon tube and centrifuge at 200×g for 30 sec. The aggregates pellet while single differentiated cells remain in the supernatant — discard the supernatant and culture the pellet.

section: HPC differentiation phase (STEMdiff™ Hematopoietic Kit, Day 0–12)
text:
HPC differentiation phase (STEMdiff™ Hematopoietic Kit, Day 0–12)






NoteMedia prep math audit





Table 1 of the STEMdiff™ Hematopoietic Kit insert specifies Medium A (45 mL Basal + 225 µL Supplement A) and Medium B (75 mL Basal + 375 µL Supplement B) — both a 1:200 (200X) supplement dilution (\(225/45{,}000 = 375/75{,}000 = 1/200\)). The calculator below applies that same 1:200 ratio to whatever basal-medium batch size you enter.





Code
viewof mediumA_basal_mL = Inputs.number({label: "Medium A — Basal Medium batch (mL)", value: 45, min: 1, step: 1})
viewof mediumB_basal_mL = Inputs.number({label: "Medium B — Basal Medium batch (mL)", value: 75, min: 1, step: 1})


















Code
supplement_ratio = 1/200   // 200X supplement, from Table 1 of the kit insert

mediumA_supp_uL = mediumA_basal_mL * 1000 * supplement_ratio
mediumB_supp_uL = mediumB_basal_mL * 1000 * supplement_ratio

Inputs.table([
  {Medium: "Medium A (Stage 1, Day 0–3)", Component: "STEMdiff™ Hematopoietic Basal Medium", Volume: `${fmt(mediumA_basal_mL,1)} mL`},
  {Medium: "Medium A (Stage 1, Day 0–3)", Component: "STEMdiff™ Hematopoietic Supplement A (200X)", Volume: `${fmt(mediumA_supp_uL,0)} µL`},
  {Medium: "Medium B (Stage 2, Day 3–12)", Component: "STEMdiff™ Hematopoietic Basal Medium", Volume: `${fmt(mediumB_basal_mL,1)} mL`},
  {Medium: "Medium B (Stage 2, Day 3–12)", Component: "STEMdiff™ Hematopoietic Supplement B (200X)", Volume: `${fmt(mediumB_supp_uL,0)} µL`}
], {layout: "auto"})






























Store complete medium at 2–8°C for up to 3 weeks, or −20°C for up to 6 months. Thaw Basal Medium at RT or overnight at 2–8°C; thaw Supplement A/B at RT or 2–8°C (centrifuge 30 sec if needed to remove liquid from the cap). Warm all media to RT before use; do not leave at RT for extended periods.

Passaging cells as aggregates & setting up HPC differentiation

Prepare Matrigel-coated plates (see iPSC culture protocol).
Perform triplicate aggregate counts: draw a “+” counting grid centered on the bottom of 3 wells of a 96-well flat-bottom plate. Aliquot 40 µL DMEM/F12 into each of the 3 wells, then add 5 µL of aggregate mixture to each. Count aggregates ≥50 µm diameter in each well; average the triplicate to get the Concentration of Cell Aggregates.
Plate 96–196 aggregates/well (10–20 aggregates/cm²) to achieve 40–80 colonies/well (4–10 colonies/cm²) adhered after 24 h — multiple plating densities may need to be tested.







TipPlating volume calculator





\[Plating\ Volume\ (\mu L) = \frac{Number\ of\ Aggregates\ to\ Plate}{Concentration\ of\ Cell\ Aggregates\ (aggregates/\mu L)}\]





Code
viewof n_aggregates_to_plate = Inputs.number({label: "Number of aggregates to plate (source range: 96–196)", value: 146, min: 96, max: 196, step: 1})
viewof aggregate_conc_per_uL = Inputs.number({label: "Your measured concentration of cell aggregates (aggregates/µL, from the triplicate count above)", value: 5, min: 0.1, step: 0.1})


















Code
plating_volume_uL = n_aggregates_to_plate / aggregate_conc_per_uL

md`**Plating volume: ${fmt(plating_volume_uL,1)} µL** of aggregate mixture per well — add to a Matrigel-coated 12-well plate containing 1 mL mTeSR1. If using split ratios instead of a counted plating volume, 1:40 to 1:200 may be required depending on confluence.`

















Gently mix the aggregate mixture; add the calculated plating volume to each Matrigel-coated well (1 mL mTeSR1 already in the well).
Place in the 37°C incubator; move in short back-and-forth/side-to-side motions to distribute aggregates; do not disturb for 24 h. Change media with mTeSR1 after 24 h; do not disturb for another 24 h. Count to confirm aggregates after 48 h.



Stage 1 — Day 0–2






WarningColony-count thresholds — discrepancy flagged in the source



The source states two different lower bounds in adjacent paragraphs: “Confirm that 80–160 colonies/well are adhered” (4–10 colonies/cm²), but then “CRITICAL: Do not proceed if cultures have < 40 colonies or > 160 colonies per well.” Both numbers are reproduced verbatim below.










Day
Step




0
Confirm 80–160 colonies/well adhered (4–10 colonies/cm²) — count all colonies, including tiny few-cell ones. To ease counting, replace medium with fresh mTeSR™1/mTeSR™ Plus/TeSR™-E8 first (removes debris). CRITICAL: do not proceed if < 40 or > 160 colonies/well (see discrepancy note above) — differentiation will be compromised.


0
Aspirate medium; add 2 mL Medium A/well. Incubate 37°C for 2 days.


2
Using a serological or 1 mL pipette, gently remove 1 mL medium/well; discard. Gently add 1 mL Medium A/well. Incubate 37°C for 24 h.





Stage 2 — Day 3–12







Day
Step




3
Aspirate medium; gently add 2 mL Medium B/well. Incubate 37°C for 2 days.


5
Gently remove 1 mL medium/well; discard. Gently add 1 mL Medium B/well. Incubate 37°C for 2 days.


7
Floating cells become visible and increase for the rest of the protocol. Keeping the plate flat, gently remove 1 mL medium/well without disturbing the floating population; discard. Add 1 mL Medium B/well. Incubate 37°C for 3 days.


10
Keeping the plate flat, gently remove 1 mL medium/well; discard. Add 1 mL Medium B/well. Incubate 37°C for 2 days.


12
Harvest hematopoietic cells (see below).









TipOptional Day 10 harvest





Cells may be harvested at Day 10 instead, as described for Day 12. Yield and the proportion of CD34+CD45+ cells will be lower than at Day 12, but CFUs may be present at a higher frequency.









NoteMedia “total required” figures don’t match the per-day add volumes





The source states Medium A total required is “1.5 mL per well” (for Day 0 + Day 2) and Medium B total required is “2.5 mL per well” (for Day 3, 5, 7, 10) — but summing the actual per-day add volumes gives 3 mL/well for Medium A (2 mL + 1 mL) and 5 mL/well for Medium B (2 + 1 + 1 + 1 mL), exactly double the stated totals in both cases.






Code
mediumA_per_well_mL = 3     // 2 mL (Day 0) + 1 mL (Day 2) — see discrepancy note above
mediumB_per_well_mL = 5     // 2 + 1 + 1 + 1 mL (Day 3, 5, 7, 10) — see discrepancy note above

Inputs.table([
  {Medium: "Medium A", "Per well (summed)": `${mediumA_per_well_mL} mL`, "Total (this batch)": `${fmt(mediumA_per_well_mL * n_wells_hpc,1)} mL`},
  {Medium: "Medium B", "Per well (summed)": `${mediumB_per_well_mL} mL`, "Total (this batch)": `${fmt(mediumB_per_well_mL * n_wells_hpc,1)} mL`}
], {layout: "auto"})

























Day 12 — Harvest hematopoietic cells







Step
Action




1
Vigorously pipette (triturate) cells up/down in the well to break them up as needed.


2
Transfer the cell suspension to a collection tube.


3
Add 1 mL DMEM/F-12 to the well; triturate vigorously and add to the collection tube.


4
Repeat step 3.


5
Centrifuge 300×g, 5 min, RT. Discard the supernatant.


6
Resuspend the cell pellet in the desired medium for analysis or downstream assays.

Add 10 mL Supplement 1 and 400 µL Supplement 2 to 90 mL Basal Medium — ratios of 10/90 and 400/90 per mL of basal, applied to whatever batch size you enter below.

Day
Step




12
Harvest suspended HPCs (Day 12 of the HPC phase above); count with Trypan Blue + hemocytometer.


12

every other day

Code
viewof mat_replate_cells = Inputs.number({label: "Cells replated (source target: 1×10⁶; minimum viable: 5×10⁵)", value: 1000000, min: 100000, step: 50000})









Code
mat_replate_density_per_cm2 = mat_replate_cells / well_area_cm2
mat_below_min = mat_replate_cells < 500000

mat_below_min
  ? md`::: {.callout-warning}
**${fmt(mat_replate_cells,0)} cells is below the 5×10⁵ minimum.** Replating density = ${fmt(mat_replate_density_per_cm2,0)} cells/cm² — continuing with fewer than 5×10⁵ cells (5.5×10⁴ cells/cm²) may reduce the %CD11b+ yield at the end of maturation.

  : md`**Replating density: ${fmt(mat_replate_density_per_cm2,0)} cells/cm²** (optimal target: 1×10⁵ cells/cm²).`






























Day
Step




36
Transfer the entire cell suspension to a 15 mL conical.


36
Add 1 mL/well 1× PBS/EDTA; incubate 4 min. Collect and transfer to the conical. Wash with another 1 mL/well PBS/EDTA; collect and add to the conical.


36
Centrifuge 300×g, 5 min. Remove supernatant, leaving ~1 mL on top of the pellet; gently resuspend. Count with Trypan Blue + hemocytometer.

NoteMath audit — how every volume is calculated





Every reagent below is dispensed per-tube at a fixed per-sample volume, so total quantity to have on hand scales linearly:
\[V_{total} = V_{per\_sample} \times N_{samples} \times (1 + overage)\]
Only Solution I + RNase A (added together and vortexed in Step 4) is realistically premixed as a shared master mix — Solutions II and III, chloroform, and ethanol are added directly per-tube during the prep, so the table below is an ordering/prep quantity calculator rather than a single combined master mix.
Ethanol precipitation volume is calculated as a configurable fraction (0.8–1×) of the ~450 µL supernatant volume carried through the two chloroform extractions, per the source protocol’s “0.8-1 volume” instruction.

NoteMath audit — how Buffer QG and isopropanol volumes are calculated





The source protocol gives the ratio directly (not derived): “Add 3 volumes Buffer QG to 1 volume gel (e.g., 100 mg gel ≈ 100 µL QG)” — i.e. 1 mg of gel slice is treated as ≈1 µL by volume (standard aqueous-gel density assumption used throughout QIAGEN kit documentation), and for 2% gels the source specifies 6 volumes instead of 3:
\[V_{QG} = k \times gel_{mg} \qquad k = \begin{cases}3 & \text{gel} \le \sim\!1.5\%\\ 6 & \text{gel} = 2\%\end{cases}\]
Isopropanol is added at “1 gel volume” — i.e. equal to the gel weight in mg treated as µL:
\[V_{isopropanol} = 1 \times gel_{mg}\]
Per-sample totals for ordering/aliquoting purposes then scale as \(V \times N_{samples} \times (1+overage)\), same convention as this notebook’s other master-mix tables.

The source protocol describes mixing Sample Buffer + DNA one tube at a time (3 µL + 1 µL). \[V_{total} = 1\;mL \times N_{vials} \times (1+overage)\] \[V_{FBS} = 0.90 \times V_{total} \qquad V_{DMSO} = 0.10 \times V_{total}\]



Freezing media (90% FBS / 10% DMSO)


Code
freeze_total_mL = 1 * scale
freeze_fbs_mL   = 0.90 * freeze_total_mL
freeze_dmso_mL  = 0.10 * freeze_total_mL
